# Web browser automation via Chrome DevTools Protocol: headless Chrome control from scripts

Curated by Skill Harbor — @mitsuhiko's web-browser skill: a minimal CDP toolkit so an agent can drive a real Chrome — launch headless with an isolated fresh profile (or a copy of your own profile, never the live one), navigate, click, fill forms, evaluate JavaScript, take viewport or full-page screenshots, emulate mobile devices (iPhone/Pixel presets), dismiss EU cookie dialogs, and capture console, error and network activity as JSONL logs with a net-summary helper. Thoughtful safety boundaries: isolated profiles by default, headed mode only when a person must see or authenticate, pick-element requires a visible window, and the skill refuses to attach to your live Chrome session. Honest caveats: needs Node.js and a Chrome/Chromium install on the agent's machine; `--profile` copy mode loads your cookies — convenient for authenticated flows, keep session hygiene in mind; the SKILL.md frontmatter jokingly says "license: Stolen from Mario" — the repo's declared license is Apache-2.0. Skill Harbor never reviews the code, review it yourself before use. Discovered via skills.sh.
